findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — [P1 confidence 100 blocking] `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW_MEMBERS, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_MEMBERS)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId());` confuse authorization-resource IDs with group-model IDs, although AdminPermissionsSchema.java:121 stores the model ID as the resource name and line 141 resolves permissions with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so enumerated resources are evaluated against the all-groups fallback and granted authorization IDs cannot identify memberships in UsersResource.java:398/450.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121 — [P1 confidence 75 blocking] `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> {` requires a type invariant that `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId());` in AdminPermissionsSchema.java:121 never establishes for individual group resources, while initialization explicitly types only the all-groups resource at line 274, so the enumeration omits resources created for specific groups and user counts cannot reflect their member-view grants.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:37 — [P2 confidence 75 advisory] `class GroupPermissionsV2 extends GroupPermissions` makes the new evaluator inherit the V1 management contract even though all nine management operations at lines 167–209 are explicitly unsupported, so every V1 management API addition requires a V2 inheritance audit to avoid silently exposing another incompatible operation; the strongest counterargument is reuse of the require/access wrappers and the existing UserPermissionsV2 precedent, but an evaluator-only base preserves that reuse while removing the invalid management relationship and those nine overrides.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:130 — [P2 confidence 75 advisory] `private boolean hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes)` duplicates the resource lookup, all-resource fallback, evaluation and scope scan in UserPermissionsV2.java:95–142, so correcting schema fallback or evaluation semantics now requires coordinated edits to independently drifting implementations; the strongest counterargument is that user checks also accept an EvaluationContext and validate returned resource IDs, but a shared evaluator accepting resource type, resource name and optional context preserves those differences and eliminates the duplicated branches at GroupPermissionsV2.java:131–164 and UserPermissionsV2.java:96–140.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:109 — [P2 confidence 75 advisory] `case GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE -> name = resolveGroup(session, id);` adds another resource-kind enumeration without extending `getResourceName`, whose sole type branch at line 334 handles Users and whose fallback is `return resource.getDisplayName();`, so newly created group resources have UUID names and no resolved group display label; the strongest counterargument is that Clients already use this fallback, but the new group writer also never supplies a display name, demonstrating that separate creation/display dispatches already drift and should share resource-type resolution metadata.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:87 — [P1 confidence 75 advisory] Adding `GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, GROUPS` leaves already-enabled realms without the Groups resource and its three new member scopes because `init()` still exits at `if (client != null) {` (line 250), so initializing an existing authorization client never provisions the schema required to create Groups permissions; the strongest counterargument is that a fresh realm receives every resource and scope, but that does not cover an existing realm retaining its Users and Clients permissions.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:109 — [P2 confidence 75 advisory] The new `case GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE -> name = resolveGroup(session, id);` stores a group ID without adding the corresponding group-name branch to `getResourceName()`, whose only model lookup remains `if (USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)) {` (line 334), so resolving a Groups permission resource never returns the group name or an All groups label and instead falls through to `return resource.getDisplayName();`; the strongest counterargument is that resource IDs suffice for permission evaluation, but that leaves the existing human-readable permission-resource representation incomplete for the new type.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — [P1 confidence 100 blocking] `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW_MEMBERS, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_MEMBERS)` passes an authorization-resource ID into the group-ID lookup `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` at line 141 even though AdminPermissionsSchema creates the resource with the group ID as its name, so a group-specific grant is evaluated against the all-groups fallback instead, and `granted.add(groupResource.getId());` additionally supplies authorization-resource IDs to the user-search and user-count callers that require actual group IDs.

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that resourceStore.findByType won't find individual group resources because they're not typed correctly. However, looking at AdminPermissionsSchema.java, the getOrCreateResource method at line 102-115 creates resources with the proper resourceType (GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE for groups) via the switch statement. The resource is created with resourceStore.create() and then resource.setType(resourceType) is called. The findByType query should find these resources. The finding misreads how resources are created and typed - individual group resources ARE typed with GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE when created through getOrCreateResource.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that GroupPermissionsV2 extends GroupPermissions (line 37) while throwing UnsupportedOperationException for all management operations (lines 167-209: isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewMembersPermission, manageMembersPermission, manageMembershipPermission, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, getPermissions). This is a valid architectural concern - the inheritance relationship includes a management contract that V2 explicitly doesn't support. The diff shows UserPermissionsV2 follows the same pattern (extends UserPermissions), providing precedent but not eliminating the concern. This is a legitimate design/architecture issue worth discussing, though not a bug since the UnsupportedOperationException throws prevent incorrect behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies code duplication between GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() (lines 130-164) and UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission() (visible in the diff at lines 95-142). Both methods follow the same pattern: check isAdminSameRealm, get ResourceServer, lookup resource by name, fallback to type resource if null, check if policies exist, evaluate permissions, and scan for matching scopes. This is a legitimate architectural/maintainability concern - changes to permission evaluation semantics would require coordinated edits to both files. However, this is a design/refactoring suggestion rather than a bug, as both implementations appear functionally correct.
